questions.stem: A young woman who is known to have pan ulcerative colitis is admitted for a severe relapse. Since there was no response to medical treatment, surgery is decided. The patient is very sceptical about surgery and requested more information. What is the appropriate way to address her concerns?

options.text: Tell her that she will die if surgery is not performed
Discard her concerns as unfounded and push her for surgery
Inform her that surgery will leave her with a colostomy bag
Agree on another meeting with the surgeon and the gastroenterologist

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man, who has been medically treated as peptic ulcer for a long time, underwent upper endoscopy, which showed a malignant ulcer. During the visit, he started blaming his primary physician and wanted to file a complaint. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Agree that it is his right to do so
Take a neutral stand in this issue
Inform him that his doctor did what he could do
Tell him that he should blame himself not his doctor

questions.stem: A married man, who had a trip to Thailand 2 months ago, is complaining of recurrent diarrhoea and weight loss. He underwent HIV testing which came reactive. However, he requested not to tell anyone including his wife. Which of the following is the best response?

options.text: Disclose the result to his emplover
Request the social worker to inform his wife
Report to the infection control unit in the hospital
Respect his request not to disclose the result to anyone

questions.stem: An elderly patient is admitted with diagnosis of unstable angina. He is known to have atrial fibrillation and taking warfarin. The attending resident administered heparin but did not check the INR, which came back as 6.8. The patient developed bleeding from the gums and hematuria. His son is upset, and he requests an explanation. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Say that you are sorry for what happened and request him to calm down
Apologize and reassure him that you will start an investigation
Tell him that this is an expected side effect of the drug
Inform him that the situation is under control

questions.stem: vessel disease requiring coronary bypass surgery. The patient refused surgery. Being the resident with the team, what is the appropriate communication tool to be used?

options.text: Use the SPIKES protocol
Tell the son to speak to the patient
Respect autonomy and continue medical treatment
Apply the counselling in the presence of the consultant

questions.stem: A patient who presented with heart failure had an echocardiogram, which showed severe rheumatic mitral regurgitation requiring valve replacement. He is waiting to know the result. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to break the news?

options.text: Avoid asking him about what he already knows
Tell him all the details from the beginning
Express more sympathy than empathy
Deliver the information in small steps

questions.stem: A 53-year-old widow with dilated cardiomyopathy presented to the Cardiology Clinic with decompensated heart failure. She lives alone, has no insurance and cannot afford the cost of medications. During counselling, which of the following is the most appropriate plan?

options.text: Arrange for a charity organization to help her financially
Involve the social worker and the hospital support system
Refer her to the Emergency Department
Advise her to avoid salt and stop smoking

questions.stem: A 79-year-old man with multiple co-morbidities is hospitalized for dissecting aneurysm and needs urgent surgery. He lives alone and he has no written will or advanced directive. His condition is very critical in the ICU. What is the best way to arrange the consent for surgery?

options.text: The attending medical team should sign the consent form
The social worker is asked to complete the consent form
Proceed for emergency and delay the consent
Request a court decision

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man known to have COPD refused the advice to stop smoking. What is the best statement should be given to him during a communication session?

options.text: "You better stop smoking otherwise you will die"
'We will do everything to help you stop smoking"
"We have to talk to your family about this refusal"
"If you don't stop smoking we will stop seeing you in the clinic"

questions.stem: A young patient has poorly controlled asthma and her doctor decided to start her on oral steroids. She is uncomfortable about that decision. When counselling this patient, what is the most important communication aspect should be addressed?

options.text: Her living conditions
The patient's concerns
Dealing with her anger
The scientific basis of using steroids

questions.stem: A 74-year-old man, who smokes for 40 years, underwent a CT chest, which showed a large lung mass.Which of the following is the most appropriate way to break the bad news?

options.text: Avoid wasting time and tell him directly that he has lung cancer
Inform him that this is nothing to worry about
Inform him that he should stop smoking
Deliver the information in small steps

questions.stem: A patient with interstitial lung disease has repeated admissions for pneumonia. His son is worried about antibiotics induced diarrhoea. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to address this situation?

options.text: Tell him that the diarrhea is not serious
Stress that the hospital infection control policy will be implemented
Agree with him that the antibiotics should be stopped
Apologize for repeatedly using antibiotics to treat his father

questions.stem: An elderly patient sustained a major stroke and he is intubated in the intensive Care Unit. However, even he was in a very critical state, he managed to write in the bed clothes that he wants to die in peace. Few days later, he passed away without resuscitation according to what he wrote. His son was very angry and said that his father had no mental capacity to decide. What is the most appropriate stand when dealing with this situation?

options.text: Find out whether the son is the real next of kin
Tell the son that in anyway his father would have never made it
Inform the son that the doctors respected the wish of your father
Inform the son that we do not resuscitate patients who are brain dead

questions.stem: A young woman is diagnosed to have multiple sclerosis. She went through an emotional breakdown during breaking bad news. Which of the following is the most appropriate way to express empathy?

options.text: “I share you your feelings and will support you"
"Pull yourself up and follow our instructions"
"I am very sorry for what happened"
"Do not worry, you will be fine"

questions.stem: A 22-year-old woman seen in the clinic with sexual function disorders. She feels uncomfortable and fearful about potentially embarrassing discoveries during examination of the breasts and genitals. She refused to be seen by a male doctor and she requested a female doctor. which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Reject
Respect
Convince
Discharge

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate action when examining a patient of different gender?

options.text: Be professional
Ask for a nurse
Build a therapeutic relationship
Expose necessary body parts only

questions.stem: A recently married woman continued taking oral contraceptive pills prescribed before her marriage for irregular menstruation. Her husband wanted his wife to discontinue the pills as he wish to have a baby, but the wife refused. Which of the following is most appropriate action?

options.text: Be empathic
Show support to wife
Show support to husband
Mutual consent required for contraception

questions.stem: A 50-year-old diabetic woman admitted to the medical ward with chest pain. The chest X-ray is suggestive of empyema. The radiologist was consulted and advised to do CT guided aspiration. Who should perform the informed consent process?

options.text: The radiologist
The head nurse
The internal medicine resident
Any member of the treating team

questions.stem: An intemal medicine resident is teaching the medical students how to examine a diabetic patient. He forgot to close the curtain while exposing the patient's abdomen. Which one of the ethical principles is violated?

options.text: Respect patients dignity
Respect patients privacy
Respect patients autonomy
Respect patients confidentiality

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man is admitted as a suspected Ebola case. After few hours, the patient asked the treating physician to discharge him or he will leave the hospital. Which of the following is the most appropriate next action?

options.text: Call the hospitals security team
Consult the hospitals ethics committee
Refer the case to the infectious disease team
Ask the patient to sign the discharge against medical advice from

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man is diagnosed with metastatic cancer. His family asked the oncologist not to tell their father of the diagnosis. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Consult the hospitals legal advisor
Inform the patient about his diagnosis
Consult the hospitals ethics committee
Do not inform the patient about his diagnosis

questions.stem: A 78-year man with post chemotherapy and radiotherapy end stage cancer is suffering from unbearable pain. His family asked the oncologist to increase the pain killer doses to relive their father's pain. The oncologist agreed after explaining to the family that the higher doses may hasten their father's death. Which of the following principles is used to make the decision?

options.text: Principle of totality
Principle of subsidiarity
Principle of double effect
Principle of informed choice

questions.stem: A 70-year-old woman admitted for a hip replacement operation. The surgeon was interrupted by the patient when he was trying to explain the surgery and its possible complications. The patient expressed her wish to not knowing the details. The surgeon respected her wish and informed the anesthesiologist who insisted to explain to the patient all details. Which of the following actions should be taken by the surgeon?

options.text: Consult the hospitals ethics committee
Let the anesthesiologist deal with the patient
Inform the patient about the anesthesiologist decision
Reschedule the operation and find another anesthesiologist

questions.stem: A 40-year-old diabetic man presents to the Emergency Room with charcot knee. He was stabilized and transferred to the Surgical Ward. The surgical team explained to the patient the need for amputation. The patient refused. Which of the following is the most appropriate next action?

options.text: Assess the patient mental capacity
Refer the patient to another hospital
Consult the hospitals clinical ethics committee
Ask the patient to sign discharge against medical advice form

questions.stem: A 20-year-old man was admitted for a simple tonsillectomy. The operation took longer time than usual because of a bleeding resulted from a surgical error. The surgery was successful and the patient fully recovered with no complications. Next day the patient asked the surgeon why his operation took longer time than usual. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Consult the hospital's ethics committee
Reassure the patient and tell him what happened
Ask another surgeon from the team to tell the patient
Reassure the patient but do not tell him what happened

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman presented to the Emergency Room with abdominal pain. The signs and symptoms are suggestive of acute appendicitis. During the surgery, the appendix found in normal state. Appendectomy was done as it is the common practice is to remove the appendix even if it is not inflamed. The surgeon does not remember that he informed the patient about this decision during the consent procedure. What should the surgeon do when the patient recovered next day?

options.text: Tell the patient that it is part of the standard procedure
Ask another surgeon from the team to tell the patient
Consult the hospital's ethics committee
Do not tell the patient what happened

questions.stem: A 90-year-old man with advanced metastatic lung cancer was admitted to the Surgical Intensive Care Unit with deteriorating pulmonary functions and labelled a do not resuscitate case by the intensivist. The thoracic surgeon would like to do a de-bulking operation to enable the patient to breath but not sure, if the patient could survive the operation, Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Explain to the patient and ask him to sign high risk consent form
Do not operate since the patient is likely not going to improve
Consult the hospitals ethics committee
Discuss the case with the intensivist

questions.stem: A 19-month-old boy known case of spinal muscular atrophy admitted with deterioration of pulmonary functions that mandate intubation. The pediatrician discussed the decision of intubation with the family but they refused because of their previous experience with their child who died with the same condition. Which of the following is the most appropriate next action?

options.text: Call the hospital's child abuse team
Search the Internet for similar cases
Consult the hospital's clinical ethics committee
Ignore the family objection and intubate the patient

questions.stem: A 15-year-old boy is a suspected case of acute meningitis was rushed to the Emergency Room by his parents. The pediatrician decided to do a lumber puncture. Which of the following is the most appropriate next action?

options.text: Take parent consent but not patient assent
Take patient assent but not parent consent
Take both patient assent and parent consent
Do not take patient assent or parent consent because it is an emergency case

questions.stem: A 12-year-old girl is brought to the Emergency Room with multiple bruises attributed by her parents to an accident while she was playing. After thorough history and physical examination, the pediatrician suspected child abuse. Which of the following is the most appropriate next action?

options.text: Call the hospital's child protection team
Confront the parents with her suspicions
Consult the hospitals clinical ethics committee
Ask the family to take the patient to another hospital

questions.stem: A newly born baby resulted from out of wedlock pregnancy was abandoned by his mother. On examination, the baby found to have inguinal heria and the pediatric surgeon advised to do hernia repair now. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Refer the case to the police **B. Refer the case to the social worker
Consult the hospitals clinical ethics committee
Perform the operation without consent form

questions.stem: A 7-year boy diagnosed with measles. When his father was asked about the child immunization record, he replayed that he does not believe in immunization. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Inform the child protection team
Consult the hospital's clinical ethics committee
Explain to the father the importance of immunization
Ignore the father's response and focus on treating the child

questions.stem: A 6-year-old child a known case of bronchial asthma presents to the Emergency Room with asthmatic attack. His father is a heavy smoker and was advised many times to avoid exposing his son to smoking. The father seems to be careless and not interested to listen to the pediatrician. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Inform the child protection team
Consult the hospital's clinical ethics committee
Explain to the father the importance of immunization
Ignore the father's response and focus on treating the child

questions.stem: A premature baby at 23-weeks, with fatal congenital anomalies is born and in need for intubation and resuscitation. His mother is one of the physicians in the hospital and she expressed her wish to do not resuscitate the baby. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Honor the mother's wish
Refer the case to another colleague
Consult the hospital's clinical ethics committee
Ignore the mother's wish and do full resuscitation

questions.stem: A 36-year-old diabetic woman presents to the clinic for a follow-up visit, and after an initial assessment, the physician wishes to perform a physical examination. He first asked her permission, which was granted. Which of the following ethical measures was the physician adopting?

options.text: Obtain informed consent
Respect for the patient
Fulfil his responsibility
Show his efficiency

questions.stem: A 40-year-old diabetic man was treated appropriately with small doses of insulin. On next follow- up visit, he bought a very expensive watch as a gesture of gratitude to his physician. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Accept and advise not to repeat
Refuse and give a warning
Politely refuse the gift
Accept from the rich

questions.stem: A 36-year-old newly diagnosed hypertensive man presents for a follow-up visit. After a thorough assessment, the physician discussed with him his diagnosis, the aetiology of his illness, the probable side effects of the prescribed medicine, the prognosis of his illness and finally, the restrictions the patient might experience due to the illness. Which of the following professional skills does the physician use?

options.text: Developing rapport
Improving communication
Providing informational care
Developing bonding with the patient

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most useful communication technique when taking a patient history?

options.text: Humour
Silent Listening
Specific questions
Open-ended questions

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of the open-ended questions in consultation?

options.text: "Tell me about the pain."
"Tell me about the pain in your chest."
"Point to the area of pain in your chest."
"Have you seen a doctor in these 6 months?

questions.stem: A 9-year-old boy just diagnosed with growth hormone deficiency. In family meeting with the child and his patents after making introductions, the doctor makes the following comment, "I'd like to go over the diagnosis, then talk about what might happen next, that's to say how you might progress. then I'll try to answer all your questions" Which of the following describes doctor phrase?

options.text: Probing
Agenda setting
Safety netting
Checking understanding

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man known to have is admitted to the Coronary Care Unit for the 5th time during the past 2 months. This admission! Ate is in refractory heart failure despite being on high doses of inotropic agents and nasal CAP, Decision is made to consider him for heart transplantation. After setting the scene, how would you break the news?

options.text: Start with a warning shot and deliver the news in small steps
Do not waste time, tell him the decision directly
Deal with his concerns by expressing sympathy
Discuss the decision with his son

questions.stem: An 80-year-old woman who presents to the clinic with a vulval lump. It has been bleeding intermittently. It is very sore and she is finding it very uncomfortable to sit down. A new vulval lump in an elderly woman is vulval cancer until proven otherwise. It is not unusual for elderly women to put off consulting their doctors because of embarrassment and reluctance to be examined. What is the best step to reduce embarrassment and reluctance to be examined?

options.text: Building rapport, taking history and examination
Getting help from social worker in management plan
Brief discussion and reschedule a visit in a nearest future
Introducing oneself followed by history and examination

questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman was seen in the clinic with her husband, they have a history of primary infertility. The investigations of the husband had showed that he is HIV positive. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Inform wife
Reassurance
Inform husband
Hide information

questions.stem: A 25-years-old pregnant woman at 20 weeks of gestation presented with twisted ovarian cyst, which needed an emergency laparotomy. The patient was explained about the condition, but she refused the surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate action should be taken?

options.text: Accept her refusal
Force her for surgery
Inform a close relative
Take the consent from husband

questions.stem: A couple with infertility came to the clinic for follow-up. The investigations showed that the wife had bilateral blocked Fallopian tubes. Which of the following is the most appropriate step of the counselling process?

options.text: Inform wife
Inform husband
Inform the couple
Inform a close relative

questions.stem: A 59-year-old woman attends to the clinic complaining of abnormal uterine bleeding for the last 2 months. All her investigations are normal and endometrial atrophy is the cause of her condition. The patient is not convinced and requesting a second opinion by another physician. Which of the following is the most appropriate response at this point?

options.text: Offer repeating the workup again
Perform further imaging studies to gain her trust
Provide a detailed medical report as it is her right
Convince her not to waste time by getting a second opinion

questions.stem: A 6-month-old girl presents to Emergency Room by ambulance with unexplained loss of conscious. Her mother appeared to have learning difficulties, and her father explained that suddenly the child went all floppy and asleep. CT brain showed subdural hemorrhage, chest x- ray showed old fractures, and eye exam showed retinal hemorrhage. After short time, the child start to cry and the parents want go home against the advice for admission. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Discharge on parent responsibilities
Discharge with follow up after 2 weeks with neurosurgery
Convince the family to continue observing her 4 hours more
Contact child protection agency and force the family to stay

questions.stem: A 78-year-old woman is admitted with fever and confusion due to pneumonia. The doctors decided to start her IV antibiotics. However, her son, who is the next of kin, disagreed and argued that antibiotics will cause more harm. What is the best way to deal with this situation?

options.text: Ignore the opinion of the son and give the antibiotics to save the patient
Counsel the son in the presence of the consultants
Respect the opinion of the next of kin
Take the opinion of the patient

questions.stem: A young woman with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis is diagnosed to have non-specific interstitial lung disease. The physician decided to start her on oral glucocorticoid. However, the patient is concerned about the side effects related to this treatment. What is the best approach to deal with this situation?

options.text: Stress the importance of the treatment and give the patient time to decide
Inform the patient that refusing this treatment might cause death C. Inform the patient that there is no alternative treatment
Tell the patient that most of the side effects are not serious

questions.stem: An elderly patient is diagnosed with pulmonary tuberculosis and started on anti-TB treatment. He developed jaundice, which progressed to liver failure for which he was admitted to the Critical Care Unit. His son was very angry and decided to complain against the treating team. What is the appropriate response to the son?

options.text: Tell him that this incident can happen to anyone
Inform him that the doctors offered the right management
Advise him against complaining as there is no medical error
Calm him down and inform him that this incident will be investigated

questions.stem: An elderly patient who has poorly controlled bronchial asthma with repeated admission to the hospital is found to be non-compliant with his medications. Which of the following is the most appropriate action? A. Tell the patient that it is not acceptable to disrespect the advice of doctors

options.text: As the patient is noncompliant, just keep him in the hospital
Involve the next of kin to help to give his medications as prescribed
Tell the patient that he might die if he does not comply with the medications

questions.stem: threatened the surgeon that he will raise a complain if did not book him for surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Do the surgery
Call the social worker
Consult the physician
Inform the administration

questions.stem: During a laparoscopic cholecystectomy, the surgeon encountered a difficult anatomy and there was a CBD injury, which was repaired and patient did very well. Which of the following is the most appropriate post-operative action?

options.text: Talk to the family
Talk to the patient
No need to tell them
Call a colleague to tell them

questions.stem: A 32-year-old man was operated for a self-induced rectal injury. After the surgery, the family was asking about the cause of his illness. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?

options.text: Inform the police
Tell them the truth
Involve social worker
Refer them to the patient

questions.stem: A 5-year-old girl brought by her family with rectal bleeding. During examination, it was observed that there is an abnormal relation between the parents. Examination confirmed multiple bruises over the child body. which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Inform the police
Admit the patient
Inform the social worker
Talk to the family about your concern

questions.stem: A 60-year-old woman was admitted for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy. During the procedure, the surgeon found a big mass in the stomach Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Cholecystectomy
Stop the procedure
Resection of the mass
Cholecystectomy and mass resection

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman who is 38 weeks of gestation refuses to have cesarean section for fetal distress. The doctor explained to her that there is a risk of fetal death, but failed to convince her to have the surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Refer to another doctor
Deliver the child vaginally
Get permission from her husband
Get permission from hospital director

questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman at 10 weeks of amenorrhea presents with heavy vaginal bleeding. She is diagnosed to have an incomplete abortion. Her husband wants to sign the consent form in place of his wife for surgery, but she refuses. Who has the right to sign the informed consent form?

options.text: Father
Doctor
Patient
Husband

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Admit for observation and call the social worker
Confirm what has happened with her husband
Discharge and advice for bed rest
Immediate cesarean section

questions.stem: A 36-year-old woman with 10-year history of infertility due to male factor is brought to Emergency Room with vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain. Thereafter, she progresses to complete abortion at 8 weeks' gestation while awaiting for admission. She is crying and her husband is an overwhelmed emotionally. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?

options.text: Quick counseling and expedite admission
Explore, identify and respond to the couple emotion
Admission to postpartum ward based on her condition
Explore, identify the cause and respond to the couple with management plan

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman G5 P0030 and her husband present to the clinic at 9 weeks' gestation with mild spotting after an intercourse, no abdominal pain reported. She has a history of 3 previous first trimester abortions. The couple are blaming themselves for the bleeding. They show a strong presentation of emotion. Which of the following is best way to deal with this situation?

options.text: Identify their emotion and calm them down
Empathic response is sufficient to calm them down
Understand their emotion without showing that to them
Explore and validate their emotion with empathic response

questions.stem: A 28-year-old G4 P0121 at 28 weeks' gestation, visitor to the country, presents with labor-like pain for 2 hours. On arrival, while trying to take history and to perform examination, the patient could not understand due to language barrier. She looks anxious and worries about her pregnancy, which is similar experience to her 4-year-old boy whom delivered prematurely. Which of the following is the most appropriate step in communication?

options.text: Showing an understanding to her emotion is inappropriate because of language barrier
Showing that her emotions cannot be validated because she had similar experience
Showing that her emotions are understood
Calling a help from other colleagues

questions.stem: A 36-year-old newly diagnosed hypertensive man presents for follow-up visit. After a thorough assessment, the physician discussed with him his diagnosis, the aetiology of his illness, the probable side effects of the prescribed medicine, and the prognosis of his illness and finally the restrictions the patient might experience due to the illness. Which of the following professional skills is the physician used?

options.text: Developing rapport
Improving communication
Providing informational care
Developing bonding with the patient

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man presented to the clinic with large thyroid nodule otherwise asymptomatic, that was proven to be papillary thyroid carcinoma. The physician is planning to send him for total thyroidectomy but the patient is afraid from the surgical complication. The treating physician needs to create a lasting impression at the end of the consultation. Which of the following is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Avoid answering all patient's questions
Patient's agreement for referral is not required
Avoid discussing the serious surgical complications
Briefly explain the action plan with possible expected and unexpected outcome

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman recently diagnosed with papillary thyroid carcinoma. Which of the following is an example of positive communication skill while explaining the management option of her disease?

options.text: Forgetting to say thank you
Ask a patient to repeat your instructions
Interrupt a patient when she ask questions
Inform patients when you cannot spend any more time with them

questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman recently diagnosed with Cushing's syndrome. which of the following will be considered as negative communication skill while explaining for her the course of her disease?

options.text: Speaking slowly with clear language
Looking directly at a patient when speaking
Interrupt a patient when he/she does not understand
Encouraging the patient to ask questions

questions.stem: A 22-year-old women presented to Surgery Clinic wearing revealing clothes, she come up very close to the doctor asking personal question in sedative tone with a language that is different from attending nurse language. Which is the following is the best response by the doctor?

options.text: Shout at here
Call the security
Refer to other doctor
Call for other nurse talk same language

questions.stem: A 70-year-old man presented with history of skin lesion over the right check (see report). Skin biopsy: Malignant melanoma. Which is the following is best way to make the patient comply with medical advice?

options.text: The illness has serous symptoms
He believes you are professional and right
Explain pathophysiology using medical terminology
Taking time to provide information and gain his trust
